local.h: UN honors CNN founder Ted Turner
local.b: The United Nations held a celebration of life for Ted Turner, who died in May at 87. His daughter Laura Turner Seydel recalled his record $1 billion gift to UN causes in 1997 and urged guests to back the institutions that hold the world together.
local.title: UN honors late media mogul and CNN founder Ted Turner

local.h: Morton Grove man died after deportation, lawyer says
local.b: Ayaz Ahmed, 61, who had chronic health conditions and needed a breathing device, died shortly after a deportation flight to Pakistan, his attorney said. He had been detained by ICE in June over an expired visa.
local.title: ‘Heartbreaking and entirely preventable’: Chicago-area man died after deportation, family attorney says

local.h: Claims center opens for Garden Grove evacuees
local.b: GKN Aerospace opened a center in Los Alamitos Tuesday to help residents evacuated during the Garden Grove chemical tank scare file for reimbursement from its $100 million claims program. Help is offered in English, Vietnamese, Spanish and Korean.
local.title: The company behind Garden Grove hazmat scare opens a center to help victims file claims

local.h: Ninth death in city jail custody this year
local.b: A man held at Rikers' Robert N. Davoren Center was found dead in his bed, at least the ninth death in Department of Correction custody this year. The department did not release a cause and will investigate.
local.title: Rikers detainee's death is at least the 9th in corrections department custody this year

local.h: Hochul keeps door open to redrawing House map
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul said Democratic gains don't necessarily end the push to amend the state constitution for mid-decade redistricting, which could let Democrats redraw New York's districts as soon as 2028, but she didn't commit.
local.title: Gov. Hochul keeps the door open to redrawing New York’s congressional map

local.h: Man indicted in killing of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors indicted a city Department of Education worker in the Oct. 30 stabbing of Katie Suarez on a Bath Beach path. Police say surveillance shows him fleeing the scene.
local.title: Man indicted in stabbing murder of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez

local.h: Judge orders city to answer ICE shelter subpoena
local.b: A federal judge ruled City Hall must give ICE the names and birthdates of South Bronx migrant shelter residents with serious criminal histories. The Mamdani administration says it is evaluating next steps.
local.title: ICE subpoena puts a spotlight on the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC

local.b: The city's Department of Transportation told a community board that concrete work on west Canal Street, planned for this fall, will slip to next year in the Reimagining Canal Street project.
local.title: Manhattan's Canal Street is getting a face-lift, but it'll take a while

local.h: East Harlem buildings head to auction despite City Hall push
local.b: Thirty-eight deteriorating buildings with about 850 mostly rent-stabilized apartments, formerly owned by bankrupt Emerald Equities Group, go to auction starting Tuesday. Mayor Mamdani's administration had backed a bid by affordable housing developer Spatial Equity to buy the portfolio first.
local.title: Rent-stabilized buildings hit auction block, despite Mamdani’s efforts to intervene

local.h: BHV Marais abruptly shuts its doors
local.b: The Paris department store closed Monday evening after an insurance policy lapsed during its bankruptcy process. Management says a new contract takes effect Tuesday, but unions fear it won't reopen.
local.title: Paris department store BHV forced to close doors

local.h: Ritz searched in Al-Fayed trafficking probe
local.b: Investigators searched the Ritz and other Paris landmarks tied to the late Mohamed Al-Fayed in a probe into accomplices in alleged human trafficking. People were held for questioning and his former Saint-Tropez estate was also investigated.
local.title: Ritz among Paris landmarks searched in Al-Fayed trafficking probe

local.h: France summons Iran's envoy over fridge sabotage
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot summoned Iran's ambassador to protest the cyberattack on supermarket fridges, calling it the first large-scale sabotage attack on French territory. He said France will push for EU sanctions and rules nothing out.

local.h: France vows tough response to Iran-blamed supermarket cyberattack
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador will be summoned and EU sanctions sought over the October attack on hundreds of supermarket fridges.

local.h: Murray questions ICE's $1.5 billion Tacoma detention deal
local.b: Sen. Patty Murray, set to chair Senate Appropriations, is pressing DHS about ICE's $1.5 billion contract to keep a private firm running the Northwest ICE Processing Center and whether ICE still plans to buy a new Seattle-area facility.
local.title: Washington state senator begins probe into deportation system after GOP loses Congress
